newsitem.title: USA: Maine seen approving $40.5 mln of ballot bonds.
newsitem.headline: Maine seen approving $40.5 mln of ballot bonds.

text.p: Maine voters appear to have approved on Tuesday a total of around $40.5 million of bond acts that appeared on the Nov 5 ballot, said a state source on Wednesday, citing unofficial results.
But the source, who declined to be named, cautioned that only around half of the vote has been counted.
"All four of them (the bond inititiatives) are ahead in the districts where they have been counted," said the state source.
He said results from some large towns, like Augusta, have not tabulated their votes yet. No further details were immediately available.
Maine's voters were asked to approve or reject the following bond initiatives.
--$16.5 million to clean up public health, hazardous substance discharge sites, including tire stockpiles, with $9 million set aside for drinking water grants for cities and towns.
--$11 million to encourage job growth and economic vitality by helping agricultural enterprises and small businesses get capital.
--$10 million to clean up water pollution and drinking water problems.
--$3 million for capital improvements at state parks.
